_comment: News source registry for the §3.11 editorial-news module. Each source is fetched by news_collector.py, classified by news_classifier.py, and stored via POST /api/admin/news. Legal rule (see NEWS_MODULE.md): we store headline + our own LLM summary + link + source + timestamp only, NEVER the source's full article body. 'coverage_weight' feeds the source-weighted tone aggregation required by TZ §3.3.

_legend.type: rss | openinfo | html | telegram — the fetcher to use
_legend.content: full = feed ships whole article (we still store snippet only); snippet = title+summary+link; none = no feed, scrape sitemap
_legend.legal: safe = reuse with attribution/link-back OK; caution = snippet+link only, respect crawl rules; avoid_fulltext = ToS bars reproduction, headline+link only
_legend.coverage_weight: 0..1 relative audience/authority weight for tone aggregation
_legend.crawl_delay_s: minimum seconds between requests to this host
_legend.max_items: per-source cap on items fetched per run, tighter than the CLI --limit (which still applies as the ceiling). Use it on whole-site feeds whose extra volume is mostly non-market news.
_legend.page_image: true = feed ships no image, so read the article page's own og:image preview tag (head only, image URL only). Omit/false when the feed already carries media:*/enclosure images, or when the page's og:image is one site-wide share card that would repeat down the feed.
_legend.feed_image: false = do NOT use even the image the feed ships (source ToS bars reuse of its media). Defaults to true.

sources.name: openinfo.uz — material facts
sources.notes: Primary issuer channel, LIVE since 2026-07-25: GET /disclosure/facts/ (newest-first, 64k+ filings, ~21/day across all ~790 filers, of which ~7/day are our listed issuers). Attributed by openinfo organization id via catalog_companies.org_id — 68 of 93 tickers have one; filings from unmapped issuers are logged and skipped, so backfilling those org_ids widens coverage. Same-issuer/same-fact-type/same-day filings are grouped into one card. Facts are marked always_relevant (skip prefilter + triage) with their tickers and §3.11 class taken from the filing itself. Covers dividends (42/50), profit-distribution recommendations (49), issuance (25/26), listing/delisting (46/47), large and affiliate deals (20-22), ownership crossings (51-53), management changes (8/9), bankruptcy (34). Reuse permitted with link-back.

sources.name: Central Bank of Uzbekistan
sources.notes: Policy-rate decisions and FX policy. Read from the press-centre listing, not the RSS: verified 2026-07-25 the feed carries a SINGLE entry (all three language variants), so a second release published between runs is lost, while the page lists ten. The listing renders an empty news__text and the article pages have no og:description, so CBU items are title-only by the publisher - do not chase a blurb. Per-article thumbnails do come from the listing; page_image stays false because its og:image is one site-wide social.jpg.

sources.name: Republican Stock Exchange Toshkent (UZSE)
sources.notes: Exchange news: listings, suspensions, new members. robots.txt bans AI-labelled UAs (GPTBot etc.) and requires a 60s crawl-delay; send a browser-style UA, never an AI-labelled one.

sources.name: Kursiv Media Uzbekistan
sources.notes: Whole-site feed (100 entries, ~79h deep): sports/entertainment/horoscopes alongside business, ~14-23 new items/day. Capped at 25 per run — raised from 15 when the schedule went to once daily, since one run now has to cover a full day's output rather than half of it. Feed ships full text; store snippet only. No featured image in the feed, but each article page exposes a real per-article og:image.

sources.name: Spot.uz
sources.notes: OOO Afisha Media, registered e-media #1207 (2019). Business focus. Feed ships its own images as rel=enclosure links (verified 2026-07-25: 10/10 items), so no page fetch is needed.

sources.name: Kun.uz
sources.notes: Largest general-news audience. Feed carries no image; the article page has an og:image. RUSSIAN feed since 2026-07-29: kun.uz was the only enabled source publishing in Uzbek, and its Uzbek headlines were the bulk of the foreign-language cards on a Russian-first feed. The language is a QUERY PARAM, not a path — /ru/news/rss and /ru/api/rss both serve the Next.js HTML page (feedparser gets 0 entries, which is what made this look impossible on 2026-07-25), while /api/rss?lang=ru returns proper XML: same 16 stories as the Uzbek feed, Russian titles, /ru/ links. Prefer the publisher's own translation over anything we could do downstream. The old /news/ URLs stay in the store as separate rows and simply age out of the 30-day window; while they are still in it they render through summary_ru like any foreign item.

sources.name: UzDaily.uz
sources.notes: Business daily. Enabled 2026-07-25: /rss serves Russian items, 20/20 with their own image, 20/20 dated, clean titles/snippets, and a high share of market news (bank assets, mortgage volumes, IMF missions, stablecoin rules) — denser signal than kursiv's whole-site feed. robots.txt explicitly allows ClaudeBot/GPTBot.

sources.name: Review.uz
sources.notes: Analytical journal, carries CERR pieces. Deferred.

sources.name: UzA — National News Agency
sources.notes: State news agency — authoritative for decrees. Deferred.

sources.name: Gazeta.uz
sources.notes: Major outlet. ToS: 'Materials may not be reproduced or distributed without prior written permission.' Headline + link + attribution ONLY, never store any article text. Feed does ship images (10/10), but under this ToS do not display them without permission — keep page_image off and treat the feed image as unusable too. Deferred.

sources.name: Daryo.uz
sources.notes: No RSS; permissive robots (only /preview/ blocked). Needs an HTML scraper. Deferred.

sources.name: КорпИнфо (Telegram)
sources.notes: ~8.3K subs, Uzbekistan capital-market wire. Read-only via public web mirror t.me/s/. Treat as a LEAD source: confirm against an openinfo fact or outlet feed before showing to users. Deferred.

sources.name: Moody's Ratings
sources.notes: Rating actions on Uzbek issuers and the sovereign. Verified 2026-07-25: Moody's publishes no usable feed, but ratingsnewsmap.xml is a rolling window of ~183 GLOBAL actions with the headline in the URL slug, and robots.txt permits it. url_filter is applied before any model call, so the ~99% naming no issuer of ours costs one shared HTTP request and nothing more. Headline only - the article pages return a 2.7KB SPA shell, and no page is opened anyway. No lastmod on these entries, so items arrive undated (kept by _is_recent, right for a window of current actions). Expect roughly one hit a week or two. Of the sister agencies, S&P stays unreachable (see the spglobal entry); Fitch turned out to BE reachable - see the fitch entry, the /page-data/ JSON its robots.txt disallows is only needed to read article pages, and we open none.

sources.name: Fitch Ratings
sources.notes: The second rating agency, read exactly like moodys. Verified 2026-07-28: /rss/press-releases and /rss/news are dead (both bounce to the /redirect/ SPA shell), but sitemap-research.xml is a live rolling set - 502 URLs the day it was checked, headline in the slug, date as a -dd-mm-yyyy suffix - and robots.txt disallows only /page-data/, /search, /redirect and /user-settings, none of which we touch since no article page is opened. Fitch does rate our market: its entity sitemap carries Asaka Bank, and the sovereign plus the state banks are all Fitch-rated, so url_filter is the same trick as moodys - the ~99.8% of global research naming nobody of ours costs one shared request. slug_date is required here: every entry's lastmod is the sitemap's own generation timestamp, so without it a five-day-old rating action would be published to readers as today's news.

sources.name: NAPP (capital-market regulator)
sources.notes: Uzbekistan capital-market regulator: licensing, the regulatory sandbox, crypto-asset and stablecoin rules, repo regulations - the primary source for the regulatory class, and it names our issuers directly (Ipak Yo'li AITB, Avesta Investment Group). Verified 2026-07-25: robots.txt is Disallow: with an EMPTY value, i.e. crawling is allowed; there is no RSS and no sitemap (every feed path returns the same catch-all HTML), so the listing page is the only machine-readable route. Titles on /ru are Russian even though the slugs are Uzbek. Publishes routine exam notices and seminars alongside real regulation, so it is deliberately NOT exempt from the relevance floor - unlike moodys, let the classifier sort it.

sources.name: The Diplomat — Central Asia
sources.notes: Regional context the local outlets do not write: reform politics, the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, energy and crypto policy. Verified 2026-07-28 - the REGION feed, not thediplomat.com/feed: both ship 96 entries, but the site-wide one is Asia-Pacific (3 mentions of Uzbekistan against 72 here) and would burn triage calls on Vietnamese AI law. Every entry is dated, carries its own image, and ships a 70-160 char teaser with no content:encoded, so snippet-only holds by construction. Volume is ~10 items per 18 days, most of them Kazakh/Kyrgyz - deliberately NOT exempt from the relevance floor, and at that rate the classifier calls are noise. robots.txt allows * everywhere but /wp-admin, while banning AI-labelled crawlers BY NAME (ClaudeBot, GPTBot, anthropic-ai, CCBot, Google-Extended, Bytespider) and setting Content-Signal ai-train=no, use=reference: our DEFAULT_UA is neutral and must stay that way, we never train on it, and we store headline + link + our own summary only.

sources.name: IMF — press releases
sources.notes: Article IV consultations, mission statements and WEO updates on Uzbekistan - a handful a year, but authoritative for the macro class. NOT deferred, blocked: checked 2026-07-28 from our network, every /en/ path (news RSS, /en/rss, /en/Countries/UZB, /en/Blogs, sitemap.xml) answers 403 Access Denied from the edge for BOTH our neutral bot UA and a full Chrome header set (Sec-Fetch-*, sec-ch-ua, Accept-Language), while /robots.txt itself returns 200 and disallows none of them. The legacy /external/ feeds (country/UZB/rss.xml, cntpst, pubs/ft/survey/sorss.xml) are all gone - they 404 into the Next.js error page. The url above is the documented feed, left here unverified. Before enabling, re-run the check from the Railway egress (a different IP may not be filtered) and confirm the feed returns XML; IMF news about Uzbekistan is in any case relayed by uzdaily and kursiv, which we already read.

sources.name: S&P Global Ratings
sources.notes: The third agency, and the only one of the three with no route at all. Re-verified 2026-07-28: www.spglobal.com answers 403 to every automated request - /robots.txt, /ratings/en/, /ratings/en/rss/index.xml alike - for our neutral bot UA and for a full Chrome header set. press.spglobal.com does answer 200 but serves an HTML press page, not a feed. Nothing here is crawl-shy behaviour we can fix with a header or a delay; enabling this needs a licensed feed. Moody's (moodys) and Fitch (fitch) cover the same rating actions on our issuers.
